extracted.intended_audience: aspiring local politicians, political operatives, and readers interested in practical street-level political strategy (early-20th-century urban machine context)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, experience-based guidance for district-level political leaders on how to win and hold power in urban machine politics: who to pick as leaders, how to behave, how to use patronage, and how to handle reformers and scandals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local roots determine loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: If he is born there and lives there only in his boyhood and then moves away, he is still beyond redemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a boy brought from Brooklyn at seven remained permanently focused on Brooklyn issues—reading a Brooklyn paper in the Assembly and ignoring his new district. Anti-pattern: trusting that early relocation erases birthplace loyalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match leader to the district
rubrics_metrics.description: Every district leader is fitted to the district he runs and he wouldn't exactly fit any other district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: choose leaders whose personalities, occupations, and manners align with local constituents. Examples: Dan Finn for janitors, Big Tom Foley for rough downtown areas, Victor Dowling (a 'hightoner') fits uptown. Avoid transplanting leaders into incompatible districts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't send outsiders (avoid Fusionist mistake)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fusionists make about the same sort of a mistake ... of sendin' men into the districts who don't know the people, and have no sympathy with their peculiarities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: appointing well-meaning but unfamiliar men into districts where they can't relate to voters (anecdote of a repeater answering as 'William Croswell Doane').

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a cosmopolitan and adapt roles
rubrics_metrics.description: I've got to be several sorts of a man in a single day, a lightnin' change artist, so to speak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice: be able to speak different registers—talk grammar with 'silk-stockins' and drop 'monkeyshines' among common people—while retaining consistent loyalty to friends and constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide jobs and favors (patronage scent)
rubrics_metrics.description: I stick to my friends high and low, do them a good turn whenever I get a chance, and hunt up all the jobs going for my constituents. There ain't a man in New York who's got such a scent for political jobs as I have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational guidance: actively locate openings (example visiting Water Register Savage at 9 A.M.), use patronage to build loyalty. Scoring: ability to secure appointments is a core measure of a leader's effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaders should be practical, not mere bookworms
rubrics_metrics.description: You hear a lot of talk about the Tammany district leaders bein' illiterate men. If illiterate means havin' common sense, we plead guilty... We don't make them district leaders. We keep them [bookworms] for ornaments on parade days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: common sense and closeness to people outweigh higher education for district leadership. Book-learned men may serve other roles but are poor district bosses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid showy style and ostentation
rubrics_metrics.description: PUTIN' on style don't pay in politics... Above all things, avoid a dress suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and anti-patterns: wearing a dress suit led a young politician to negligence, social excess, drinking, and dismissal. Rumors of an expensive automobile or dress suit can lose votes; voters resent perceived social elevation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't show off learning; speak the people's language
rubrics_metrics.description: If you're makin' speeches in a campaign, talk the language the people talk. Don't try to show how the situation is by quotin' Shakespeare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: avoid academic quotations or learned displays in campaigning. If you must indulge, do so only in private; publicly use straightforward, local speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational fit: treat the machine as specialized parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Tammany Hall is a great big machine, with every part adjusted delicate to do its own particular work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: assign people to roles that suit their strengths; the smooth operation of the machine depends on role specialization and fitting leaders to districts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural adaptability across ethnic/religious lines
rubrics_metrics.description: He is as popular with one race as with the other. He eats corned beef and kosher meat with equal nonchalance, and it's all the same to him whether he takes off his hat in the church or pulls it down over his ears in the synagogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices: demonstrate cultural fluency and avoid alienating groups; shared customs and everyday gestures build cross-group support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal ownership is desirable only after ending civil service
rubrics_metrics.description: I AM for municipal ownership on one condition: that the civil service law be repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: municipal ownership would create many jobs for the machine, but civil service would block patronage; therefore repeal civil service first. Policy sequencing is a strategic criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose civil service examinations (they cripple patronage)
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be all a mess if every man who wanted a job would have to run up against a civil service examination... Before the would-be motorman left the civil service room, the chances are he would be a raving lunatic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: merit examinations that require irrelevant learned knowledge. Claim (used as argument): more civil service reformers than politicians are found in prisons (used rhetorically to discredit reformers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use municipal control to raise salaries and loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Municipal ownership would increase them all along the line and would stir up such patriotism as New York City never knew before... When a man has a good fat salary, he finds himself hummin' 'Hail Columbia.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: higher public salaries create loyalty and civic pride; salary levels are a tool for political cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward newly formed reform 'Democracies'
rubrics_metrics.description: I've seen more than one hundred 'Democracies' rise and fall... Any man with $50 can now have a 'Democracy' of his own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence: detailed cost breakdown of creating a fake 'Democracy' and examples where such organizations secured lucrative appointments; implication: judge new political groups by their sponsors and track record, not rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: The press is gullible about small reform outfits
rubrics_metrics.description: Isn't some of the papers awful gullible about politics? ... The New York papers tumble over one another to give columns to any new organization that comes out against Tammany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational note: be aware that media attention to a new outfit does not equal genuine mass support; such publicity can be exploited by organizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: It's acceptable to profit from legislation that benefits the district
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Remsen Bill... I went in and got options on a lot of the property around the gashouses... If it had succeeded, I guess I would have been accused of graftin'. What I want to know is, what do you call it when I got left and lost a pot of money?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defense: legislators may lawfully or acceptably take financial positions that align with public improvements; caution: optics can invite accusations of graft even if motives claim to be district-improvement plus private interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't rush to accuse fellow politicians of graft
rubrics_metrics.description: Just here I want to say one last final word about civil service... don't make up your mind that a man, occupyin' the exalted position... has done wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: allow time and context before labeling actions corrupt; public perception may punish slander but certain slanders (like dress suits) have disproportionate electoral impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tammany supplies votes and cash; other regions often abstain
rubrics_metrics.description: Tammany's got the votes and the cash. The Hill crowd's only got hot air... The Democrats there—always providin' that there is any Democrats there—take to the woods [on fundraising and election day].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational implication: rely on urban organizational capacity for turnout and financing; don't expect upstate or external groups to carry local campaigns financially or electorally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufactured reform groups can be rewarded with plum offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The New York State Democracy in 1897 landed a Supreme Court Justiceship for the man who manufactured the concern—a fourteen-year term at $17,500 a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence: newly formed organizations have historically traded support for high offices, indicating political entrepreneurship and transactional politics.
